standard.title: Dance across cultures, times and places
standard.description: explore where, why and how dance is choreographed and/or performed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify where, why and how people experience dance across cultures and communities (Y1-2). They can observe and describe dance features using learnt terminology.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore where, why and how dance is choreographed and/or performed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts.

nodes.label: Purposes and meanings of dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe different purposes for which dance is choreographed and performed across cultures and times.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least two different purposes for dance from at least two different cultural or temporal contexts.
nodes.typical_width: Identifying meaning and purposes across a range of dances: cultural celebration, narrative storytelling, entertainment, ceremony; exploring dances from local community and/or countries in Asia; noting dances created for entertainment ('dance crazes', widely known dances).
wider: Investigate a dance craze or widely known dance — tracing its origin, spread, and transformation across different cultural contexts
Explore dances from a country or region in Asia — identifying their cultural purpose, the occasions on which they are performed, and what they communicate

response_modes.reason: Understanding purposes requires genuine range — single-context exposure produces single-context understanding. Ensure dances encountered span multiple purposes (not all celebrations, not all entertainment).

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who encounter dance purposes across genuinely diverse cultural and temporal contexts develop an analytical lens for dance as cultural practice — not just as performance. This supports increasingly sophisticated engagement with cultural context in Y5-6 and Y7-8.
success_criteria: Student can describe at least two different purposes for which dance is created and performed
Student can identify at least one dance from a cultural context different from their own and explain its purpose

nodes.label: Comparing dance across contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare dances from different cultures, times or places — identifying similarities and differences and asking questions about what they observe.
nodes.minimum_width: Comparing two dances from different cultural or temporal contexts — identifying at least one similarity and one difference.
nodes.typical_width: Using Viewpoints questions ('Are the movements similar to movements in dances you know?', 'Where are these dances performed?') to explore and compare dances across cultures, times and places; identifying movement similarities and differences; connecting observations to context.
wider: Investigate how a dance tradition has changed over time — exploring how context, purpose or materials have evolved while the dance persists
Explore dances from two countries in Asia and compare how they reflect cultural values, stories or occasions

response_modes.reason: Comparison requires a frame — use Viewpoints questions to structure observation before students attempt to compare. Name what they are looking for: movements, music, costume, setting, purpose, audience relationship.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one similarity and one difference between two dances from different cultural or temporal contexts
Student generates at least one question about what they have observed in a dance from an unfamiliar context
